text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your episodes of dizziness and vertigo in detail, including when they started, how long they last, and if you experience other symptoms like hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea.

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The presentation of sudden, position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old woman is classic for canalolithiasis. I would like to confirm the specific head movements that trigger the episode and ask if you have noticed any new visual disturbances or neck pain before I recommend the Dix-Hallpike maneuver for confirmation.
